concept.name: Event-Driven Architecture & Message Streaming
concept.tagline: Decouple microservices using distributed commit logs, message queues, and event streams.

spark.summary: Event-driven architecture replaces synchronous REST HTTP calls with asynchronous event publishing (Kafka/RabbitMQ), ensuring high throughput and fault isolation.
spark.keyTakeaway: Use append-only distributed logs (Kafka) for durable replayable streams.

concept.whyItMatters: Direct HTTP microservice chains create cascading failure risks.
keyPoints: Pub/Sub broadcasts events to multiple subscribers.

questions.title: Message Ordering in Distributed Log Partitions
questions.prompt: How does Apache Kafka guarantee strict sequential ordering for messages delivered to consumers?

options.text: It uses a single global lock across all cluster brokers.
options.explanation: Global locks destroy distributed log throughput.

options.text: It routes messages with the same partition key to a single partition, where they are appended sequentially to a single log.
options.explanation: Correct! Sequential ordering is guaranteed per partition key.

rubric.excellent: Explains partition keys and single-partition log append ordering.
rubric.gap: Thinks global ordering across all partitions is default.

questions.sampleSolution: Kafka guarantees message order within a single partition by routing messages with identical partition keys to that partition.
questions.explanation: Per-partition sequential log appends preserve order without bottlenecking the entire cluster.

interviewProblems.title: Reliable E-Commerce Order Processing Pipeline
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: You are designing the order processing backend for an e-commerce platform during Black Friday. When a customer places an order, 5 downstream services (Inventory, Billing, Shipping, Analytics, Fraud) must process it. How do you ensure high throughput and zero lost orders if Shipping goes down?

dimensions.name: Asynchronous Decoupling
dimensions.description: Publishing OrderPlaced events to Kafka topic instead of blocking HTTP.

dimensions.name: Idempotency & Retry Safety
dimensions.description: Handling duplicate message delivery using idempotent consumer keys.

interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Publish OrderPlaced events to a durable Kafka topic with 7-day retention. Each downstream service consumes from its own consumer group. If Shipping fails, its consumer offset pauses while other services continue unimpeded.
commonPitfalls: Chaining synchronous HTTP calls from Payment -> Inventory -> Shipping.
